posts.headline: Ten straight editions of buildup and now The Thicks actually has a roster on paper — time to find out if #FreeMaxx Champions is a dynasty or a one-hit wonder.
posts.detail: A 14-14 career record and a 5.5 average finish are backing up that lone ring, and now that the picks are locked, there's nowhere left to hide from the 2026 title defense.

posts.headline: One Nut Barner has dodged seventeen straight editions of heat, but a 20-8 career mark and back-to-back top-2 finishes with ZERO rings is the definition of a Cowboys-style choke waiting to happen.
posts.detail: Best average finish in the entire league at 1.5, yet somehow still hunting for that first title — the draft's closed, Put it in Ra, so let's see if the resume finally matches the hardware this year.

posts.headline: talentedtenthh finished a draft from the deepest hole in the league and the untalented tenth still has to prove it wasn't just rearranging deck chairs on a sinking 4-10 ship.
posts.detail: A dead-last 12th-place finish and a .286 win rate is the floor — any direction from here is technically progress, but Chauncey has to actually show it on the roster.

posts.headline: Six editions deep and Big Head's championship banner is STILL getting the fluke treatment — a losing 13-15 career record under a ring is exactly the kind of paradox that keeps this beef alive.
posts.detail: Sasinci's World owns a title but a 5.5 average finish and a below-.500 record says Megamind has been living off one great run — prove it wasn't the ceiling, Saso.

posts.headline: Eight straight editions of burial later, SwooshAnoosh finally has a full roster and zero excuses left — an 11th-place, 5-9 debut doesn't get erased by good vibes alone.
posts.detail: Dead last in career average finish among most of this league at 11, the Prince of Persia needs this draft class to actually hit, or the silence turns into a permanent sentence.
